sources.scope: Reference scope for slow IV, 20–40 mg per adult injection, the >50 mg infusion remark, and digoxin interaction. The same monograph lists an indication-specific 80 mg slow injection escalation; these statements do not establish a universal route or rate. The exam names the general recommendation only.
Earlier oral timing and volume, BP, electrolyte and renal precautions.
Pulmonary congestion with volume overload; reassess urine output and respiratory status.
Potassium-depleting drugs and increased risk of digoxin toxicity.
Indication, product-specific administration, renal and electrolyte monitoring, volume depletion and ototoxicity. Reference label does not establish a Nasser Medical Complex protocol.
Furosemide inhibition of NKCC2 measured in rat medullary thick ascending limb.
